Discounted Free Cash Flow (DCF)
Enterprise Value = PV (FCF) = Equity + Debt – Cash
Value of Equity = PV (FCF) + Cash - Debt

PV (FCF) = PV of cash flows from prior investments + NPV of future investments

Free Cash Flow in year t is calculated as:
FCFt = EBITt (1- τ) + Dept – CapExt – ΔNWCt = EBITt (1- τ) – (CapExt – Dept) – ΔNWC

Cashflows: explicit forecasting:

• Allows incorporation of changing investment opportunities, etc
• No need to directly consider dividend policy or financing

Portfolio Choice: Risk and Return
Probability distribution
When projects are risky, there are different returns that a given project may earn:
• Each possible return has some likelihood of occurring (ex. beliefs)
• This information is summarized with a probability distribution, that assigns a probability, PR, that each
possible return, R, will occur.

Expected Return
Given the probability distribution of returns, we can calculate the expected return of an investment. The
expected or mean return is calculated as a weighted average of the possible returns, where the weights

are taking. The risk, and therefore the risk premium, will vary by security
The firm’s overall cost of capital is the weighted-average cost of all sources of funding

Consider the following: The cost of debt financing is lower than the cost of equity financing. Does this imply
that debt is better?

A Common View: Debt is Cheap

WRONG!!

Adding leverage increases the risk of equity. The initial cash flows go to debt holders: first to collect. As a
result, both the volatility and the beta of equity increase
To compensate equity holders, the expected return on equity also increases!
The risk premium double when the risk double.

But, changes in the capital structure do not affect the WACC

With no debt, the WACC is equal to the unlevered equity cost of capital. As the firm borrows at the low cost of
capital for debt, its equity cost of capital rises: the net effect leaves the WACC unchanged.

M&M and WACC
You can’t shift to a lower cost of debt to decrease the WACC because the equity cost of capital is going to
increase to compensate equity holders for a higher risk.
How you purchase something doesn’t affect its the value. The pizza is the same!

Continuation or Terminal Value:
• Beyond a 5 to 10-yr horizon, our forecasts are unlikely to be precise
• Strong tendency of firms to mean-revert to industry norms
• Use a “multiples” approach to estimate value beyond the forecast horizon, based on expected long-run
growth rate. Terminal multiple is a statement of the future profitability of the firm and its industry


Multiples Valuation Procedure
• Step1: Identify firms that are considered to be the same as the firm you wish to value, the comparable firms.
• Step2: Determine relevant financial ratios for the comparable firms.
• Step3: Calculate average of the financial ratios for the set of comparable firms.
• Step4: Review and modify the set of comparable companies as necessary. Analyze the subject and
comparable companies to compare and contrast them in terms of both financial and economic characteristics.
